name: Tents
rules: Every tree needs its own tent directly beside it, never diagonally. Tents never touch, not even at corners. The numbers count the tents in each row and column.
technique.1: No tree next to this cell still needs a tent, so this cell can't hold one.
technique.2: A tent already touches this cell, so this cell can't hold one.
technique.3: This tree has only one cell left where its tent can go, so that cell must be a tent.
technique.4: This tree's tent must go in one of two cells, and both of them touch this cell, so this cell can't hold a tent.
technique.5: Only these cells in this row or column can still take a tent, and every way of fitting in the ones it needs agrees about the marked cells, so you can fill them in.
technique.6: Only these cells in this row or column can still take a tent, and every way of fitting in the ones it needs puts one next to the marked cells, so you can rule them out.
technique.7: This row or column needs as many tents as it has cells left that could hold one, so every one of them is a tent.
technique.8: This row or column already has all its tents, so no other cell in it can hold one.
demo.1: Every tree needs its own tent in a cell beside it. The numbers count the tents in each row and column.
demo.2: A tent goes directly beside its tree, above, below, left or right. Corners do not count, so these cells stay empty.
demo.3: This column needs one tent, and only one cell is left for it.
demo.4: Tents never touch, not even at a corner. These two do, so one of them has to move.
demo.5: Only one cell beside this tree is still free, so its tent goes there.
demo.6: Every tree has a tent beside it, no two tents touch, and the counts all match.
